headline: Brent jumps to $116 on Houthi attacks; Dow −1.2% as selling moves from tech to blue chips
summary: A broad but orderly decline. The Dow opened about 1% lower and stayed there, while the Nasdaq briefly turned positive on a chip rebound before slipping into the red late; the S&P 500 finished near its low. Nearly three in four S&P 500 stocks fell and decliners led advancers about 1.7 to 1 on the NYSE, with staples, consumer discretionary, financials and telecoms the weakest groups while energy hit a record and tech edged up.
drivers: Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites and an oil spill reported off the UAE sent Brent up 3.1% to $116.72, its highest settle since April, and WTI up 3.8% to $103.27. Consumer sentiment hovered near a record low on rising prices; energy stocks rose 2.5% to a record, with SLB up about 7% on a profit beat and Chevron up 2.9%.

Defensive and old-economy names that held up on Thursday gave ground: staples, discretionary and financials each fell more than 1%. American Express lost 3.7% despite a raised forecast as it announced 5% job cuts, JPMorgan and Citi fell 1.5%, Caterpillar 2.4% and Eli Lilly 2.5%.

The SOX recovered 0.44% after Thursday's 6.7% plunge and S&P tech rose 0.35%. Memory led: Micron gained 2.5% and SK hynix about 4% after it dropped the Solidigm IPO review; AMD and Intel rose 1.7%, while Nvidia slipped about 0.6% and Apple briefly passed it in market value.

A report that SpaceX is seeking access to thousands of US cell sites for a fourth wireless carrier sank AT&T and T-Mobile about 8% and Verizon 1.2%, while tower owners Crown Castle (+9%) and American Tower (+4%) rallied. Cybersecurity stocks jumped 6–8% on fresh AI-found software flaws; Bloom Energy fell 11% after results.
week: For the week: Russell 2000 +2.0%, Dow +0.4% (third weekly gain), S&P 500 −0.5% (second weekly loss), Nasdaq −0.7%, as Meta's spending shock and oil near post-war highs outweighed earnings tracking more than 30% growth. The 10-year yield still fell about 11bp on the week, staying just under 5%.
watch: Next: a third of the S&P 500 reports, including Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon, whose AI capex plans are in focus; the Fed decides Oct 28 alongside SK hynix results, Intel reports Oct 29, and the Nov 3 midterms follow.
